Raw.Title: Image user should not be 'root'
Raw.Description: Running containers with 'root' user can lead to a container escape situation. It is a best practice to run containers as non-root users, which can be done by adding a 'USER' statement to the Dockerfile.
Raw.Message: Specify at least 1 USER command in Dockerfile with non-root user as argument

Raw.Title: No HEALTHCHECK defined
Raw.Description: You should add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your docker container images to perform the health check on running containers.
Raw.Message: Add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your Dockerfile

Raw.Title: Can elevate its own privileges
Raw.Description: A program inside the container can elevate its own privileges and run as root, which might give the program control over the container and node.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation' to false

Raw.Title: Default capabilities: some containers do not drop all
Raw.Description: The container should drop all default capabilities and add only those that are needed for its execution.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should add 'ALL' to 'securityContext.capabilities.drop'

Raw.Title: Default capabilities: some containers do not drop any
Raw.Description: Security best practices require containers to run with minimal required capabilities.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of 'deployment' 'wanaware-api' in 'default' namespace should set securityContext.capabilities.drop

Raw.Title: CPU not limited
Raw.Description: Enforcing CPU limits prevents DoS via resource exhaustion.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'resources.limits.cpu'

Raw.Title: Runs as root user
Raw.Description: Force the running image to run as a non-root user to ensure least privileges.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'securityContext.runAsNonRoot' to true

Raw.Title: Image tag ":latest" used
Raw.Description: It is best to avoid using the ':latest' image tag when deploying containers in production. Doing so makes it hard to track which version of the image is running, and hard to roll back the version.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should specify an image tag

Raw.Title: Root file system is not read-only
Raw.Description: An immutable root file system prevents applications from writing to their local disk. This can limit intrusions, as attackers will not be able to tamper with the file system or write foreign executables to disk.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem' to true

Raw.Title: CPU requests not specified
Raw.Description: When containers have resource requests specified, the scheduler can make better decisions about which nodes to place pods on, and how to deal with resource contention.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'resources.requests.cpu'

Raw.Title: Memory requests not specified
Raw.Description: When containers have memory requests specified, the scheduler can make better decisions about which nodes to place pods on, and how to deal with resource contention.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'resources.requests.memory'

Raw.Title: Memory not limited
Raw.Description: Enforcing memory limits prevents DoS via resource exhaustion.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'resources.limits.memory'

Raw.Title: Runs with UID <= 10000
Raw.Description: Force the container to run with user ID > 10000 to avoid conflicts with the host’s user table.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'securityContext.runAsUser' > 10000

Raw.Title: Runs with GID <= 10000
Raw.Description: Force the container to run with group ID > 10000 to avoid conflicts with the host’s user table.
Raw.Message: Container 'api' of Deployment 'wanaware-api' should set 'securityContext.runAsGroup' > 10000

Raw.Title: Runtime/Default Seccomp profile not set
Raw.Description: According to pod security standard 'Seccomp', the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile must be required, or allow specific additional profiles.
Raw.Message: Either Pod or Container should set 'securityContext.seccompProfile.type' to 'RuntimeDefault'

Raw.Title: Seccomp policies disabled
Raw.Description: A program inside the container can bypass Seccomp protection policies.
Raw.Message: container "api" of deployment "wanaware-api" in "default" namespace should specify a seccomp profile

Raw.Title: Container capabilities must only include NET_BIND_SERVICE
Raw.Description: Containers must drop ALL capabilities, and are only permitted to add back the NET_BIND_SERVICE capability.
Raw.Message: container should drop all

Raw.Title: Workloads in the default namespace
Raw.Description: Checks whether a workload is running in the default namespace.
Raw.Message: deployment wanaware-api in default namespace should set metadata.namespace to a non-default namespace

Raw.Title: Default security context configured
Raw.Description: Security context controls the allocation of security parameters for the pod/container/volume, ensuring the appropriate level of protection. Relying on default security context may expose vulnerabilities to potential attacks that rely on privileged access.
Raw.Message: container wanaware-api in default namespace is using the default security context

Raw.Title: Restrict container images to trusted registries
Raw.Description: Ensure that all containers use images only from trusted registry domains.
Raw.Message: Container api in deployment wanaware-api (namespace: default) uses an image from an untrusted registry.
